title: Best Frigidaire Dehumidifier (2026): 50-Pint, 22-Pint & Wi-Fi
dek: The big-box brand with the most pump options — once you crack its model-number code, there's a Frigidaire for nearly every damp room.
description: The best Frigidaire dehumidifier for 2026, from the 50-pint Wi-Fi FHDD5034Y1 to pump and 22-pint models, plus error codes, manuals and filters.
intro: Walk into almost any home-improvement store in early summer and you'll find a wall of Frigidaire dehumidifiers. That shelf presence isn't an accident: the brand builds sturdy, wheeled cabinets with roomy buckets, and it offers more built-in-pump models than nearly any other consumer name. Picking the best Frigidaire dehumidifier comes down to the naming: FFAD, FHDD, FHDP, FFAP and FGAC all look alike on a price tag, and the differences between them matter.

The good news is that Frigidaire's old weak spot — power draw — has largely closed. The current 50-pint Wi-Fi model is specced at about **470 watts**, close enough to Midea's Cube that running cost is no longer the tiebreaker. That leaves the real questions: Do you need a pump? Do you want an app? And is the space a whole basement or a single bedroom?
Below are the six Frigidaire models we'd consider in 2026, what separates them, and a cheat sheet for reading Frigidaire's model numbers so you never pay extra for a suffix.
topPicksLead: For most homes, the **Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1** is the one to buy: 50 pints, Wi-Fi, a big bucket and defrost down to 41°F, without the Gallery premium.

products.name: Frigidaire 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Wi-Fi (FHDD5034Y1)
pros: ENERGY STAR certified with a specced draw of about 470 watts
Wi-Fi app plus Alexa and Google Home control
Large 2.7-gallon bucket or continuous-drain hose
Auto-defrost keeps it running down to 41°F
cons: No pump, so drainage relies on gravity
Bulky for a bedroom or small office
products.whyWeLoveIt: This is the Frigidaire you buy once and stop thinking about. It pairs a full 50-pint rating with a generous bucket, a drain-hose port and app control, so you can check the tank or nudge the humidity target without walking downstairs.
products.performance: Frigidaire rates it for spaces up to about 4,500 square feet, which covers a typical basement, garage or an entire floor. Its spec sheet lists 8.8 amps, roughly 470 watts — a meaningful improvement over the older W1 generation and close to Midea's 50-pint Cube. The Y1 suffix marks the newer R-32 refrigerant build of the same machine. Owners mainly praise the bucket size and casters; the most common gripe is the cabinet's size.

products.name: Frigidaire Gallery 50-Pint Wi-Fi Dehumidifier with Pump (FGAC5045W1)
pros: Built-in pump drains up and out of a basement
Strong water removal in published third-party testing
Pull-up handle and casters for moving it around
Ionizer and full app and voice-assistant support
cons: Heavy to carry up and down stairs
Costs noticeably more than the FHDP pump model
products.whyWeLoveIt: The Gallery is Frigidaire's flagship, and the pump is the headline. Instead of relying on a drain that sits lower than the machine, it pushes condensate through a hose to a window, sink or overhead line — which is exactly what most basements need.
products.performance: In one widely cited 2026 magazine roundup, the Gallery pulled 22.3 pints of water in four hours, the most of any unit in that test. It also offers gravity drainage and a sump-drain option, so you can pick whichever route suits the room. Owners consistently flag the weight as the only real usability complaint. Retail availability has narrowed, so expect to shop around.

products.name: Frigidaire 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Built-In Pump (FHDP5033W1 / FHDP5033Y1)
pros: Pump lifts water up to 16.4 feet
Wi-Fi scheduling and custom humidity targets

products.whyWeLoveIt: For most basements this is the smartest Frigidaire buy. You get the same practical benefit as the Gallery — a pump that moves water uphill — plus Wi-Fi scheduling, without paying for the flagship's extras.
products.performance: Frigidaire rates the pump for 16.4 feet of vertical lift, enough to clear a basement window or reach a laundry sink. The spec sheet lists 545 watts and 49 dBA, and an operating range of 41–89°F at 30–80% relative humidity. Newer stock ships as the FHDP5033Y1, the same machine on R-32 refrigerant. Compare it with every brand's self-draining units in our [dehumidifiers with a pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.

products.name: Frigidaire 50-Pint ENERGY STAR Dehumidifier (FFAD5034W1)
pros: Same 50-pint capacity and coverage as the Wi-Fi model
ENERGY STAR certified
Front-loading bucket and continuous-drain port

products.whyWeLoveIt: App control earns its keep when a dehumidifier lives somewhere you rarely visit. In a laundry room or workshop you pass daily, it doesn't. The FFAD5034W1 gives you the same capacity and certification with a plain control panel and a lower price.
products.performance: It's the plain-vanilla version of the 50-pint platform: front-loading bucket, drain-hose port, casters and the same rated coverage. Hook up a hose to a lower drain and it runs unattended just like its Wi-Fi sibling. It typically sells for noticeably less than the connected model, which makes it a good fit for anyone who'd rather glance at a display than open an app.

products.name: Frigidaire 22-Pint Dehumidifier (FFAD2233W1)

products.whyWeLoveIt: If your damp problem lives in one room, a 50-pint machine on low isn't the same as a small one sized correctly. This 22-pint model is the Frigidaire to choose for a bedroom or office, and it's noticeably quieter than its bigger siblings.
products.performance: Frigidaire lists 22.6 pints a day and rates it for roughly 330 square feet. One independent reviewer recorded 44.6 dB on low fan from 10 feet away — below normal conversation. Owners like the speed and the low draw, but a recurring theme in reviews is durability, so it's a lot of machine for the money rather than a ten-year investment. See how it stacks up in our [best small dehumidifier](/best/best-small-dehumidifier/) picks.

products.whyWeLoveIt: After a leak, a soggy spring or in a basement that never quite dries, you want a machine that keeps going without anyone emptying a tank. The FFAP5033W1 pairs Frigidaire's High Humidity setup with a pump, so water leaves the room as fast as it collects.
products.performance: It shares the 50-pint capacity, casters and filter design of the 5033/5034 family. The EPA notes mold can start on damp materials within 24 to 48 hours, which is why an unattended pump matters more than a slightly bigger bucket. For real flood cleanup, step up to a restoration-grade unit from our [commercial dehumidifier](/best/best-commercial-dehumidifier/) list.
products.notes: Frigidaire is one of the few consumer brands that sells a disposable replacement filter. Our [replacement filter guide](/guides/dehumidifier-replacement-filter/) lists part numbers.

blocks.text: That last figure is worth remembering. Below about 41°F, any compressor dehumidifier starts to ice over and stalls. Most finished and semi-finished basements stay warmer than that, but an unheated garage or a winter crawl space may not — and those spaces need a low-temperature specialist from our [crawl space](/best/best-crawl-space-dehumidifier/) or [garage](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-garage/) guides.

We don't run a test lab. We start with data that compares fairly across brands: capacity under the 2019 DOE test procedure, ENERGY STAR certification, and Frigidaire's own spec sheets and manuals for wattage, pump lift, operating temperature and drainage. Where independent publications have published water-removal or noise results, we note them and say where they came from.

Then we read owner reviews for recurring patterns — pumps that quit, sensors that misread, buckets that leak — and check the CPSC recall database. For this guide we weighted drainage first (pump versus gravity), then right-sizing, efficiency and smart features.

sections.heading: What to look for in a Frigidaire dehumidifier

items.label: Pump or gravity first
items.text: If the unit will sit below the nearest drain — true of most basements — buy a pump model (FGAC, FHDP or FFAP). Everything else is secondary.

items.label: The right capacity
items.text: A 22-pint model suits a single room; the 50-pint models cover a basement or a full floor. Our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) maps pints to square footage.

items.label: App only if you'll use it
items.text: Wi-Fi is worth paying for in a crawl space or basement you rarely visit, and nearly worthless in a room you walk through daily.

items.label: Temperature range
items.text: Auto-defrost to 41°F covers most basements. Colder spaces need a low-temp or desiccant unit.

items.label: Ignore suffix churn
items.text: A W1 and a Y1 of the same model are the same machine; Y1 typically means R-32 refrigerant. Buy whichever is cheaper and in stock.

sections.heading: How to read a Frigidaire model number

blocks.text: Frigidaire's naming looks random, but it follows a pattern. Break any model into three parts and you'll know what you're looking at.

items: **FFAD** — the standard line: reliable, no Wi-Fi, lowest price.
**FHDD** — High Humidity with Wi-Fi, like our top pick.
**FGAC** — Gallery, the premium tier with a pump, ionizer and best build.
**The digits** give capacity: 5033 and 5034 are 50-pint; 2233 is 22-pint.
**The suffix** (W1, Y1) is a revision, not a new product.

blocks.text: Midea's Cube family still wins on compact, stackable design and lift-off tank convenience. Frigidaire wins on bucket size, sturdy casters, the breadth of its pump range and a five-year sealed-system warranty. With the 50-pint Frigidaire now specced near the Cube's draw, efficiency is roughly a wash. Our head-to-head [Midea vs. Frigidaire](/compare/midea-vs-frigidaire-dehumidifier/) comparison digs into power figures and warranty terms, and [Frigidaire vs. Honeywell](/compare/frigidaire-vs-honeywell-dehumidifier/) covers the other common big-box matchup.

sections.heading: Frigidaire dehumidifier repair, error codes, manuals and filters

blocks.text: Frigidaire displays two-letter codes when something stops the cycle, and the exact meaning varies by model and generation. Codes such as **EC** generally point to a sensor or sealed-system fault rather than something you can fix, while codes tied to the bucket usually clear once the tank is emptied and seated properly. **F0/FO** codes are among the most searched. Before calling for service, try the basics below, then check the code table in your model's manual.

items: Unplug the unit for five to ten minutes to reset the control board.
Empty the bucket and reseat it firmly; a tilted or loose bucket trips the full-tank switch.
Clean the filter and make sure the room is above 41°F so the coils aren't icing.
Plug back in and watch whether the code returns; a repeat code usually means a service call.

blocks.text: The model number is printed on a label on the back or side of the cabinet, often behind the bucket. Search that full number, suffix included, on Frigidaire's support site to download the user manual, warranty terms and parts diagrams. Older models like the **FFAD5033R1**, **FFAD3033R1** and **FAD504DWD** are earlier generations that have been replaced by the current W1 and Y1 lineup; if you own one, also run its model number through the CPSC recall database.

Most Frigidaire models use a washable mesh filter behind the front grille; rinse it every two weeks during heavy use. Some High Humidity models also accept a disposable OEM filter. Our [replacement filter guide](/guides/dehumidifier-replacement-filter/) lists part numbers, and our [maintenance guide](/guides/dehumidifier-maintenance/) covers coil cleaning and storage. If the unit runs but won't pull water, start with [dehumidifier not collecting water](/guides/dehumidifier-not-collecting-water/).

The **Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1** is the best Frigidaire for most homes: 50 pints, Wi-Fi, a big bucket and defrost to 41°F. If your unit will sit below the drain, go straight to a pump model — the **Gallery FGAC5045W1** for the strongest performer, or the **FHDP5033W1** for the same 16.4-foot lift for less. The **FFAD5034W1** trims the app to save money, and the **FFAD2233W1** is the quiet single-room answer. Prices on the same model can vary widely across retailers, so check two or three before you buy, and see how Frigidaire ranks overall in our [best dehumidifier brands](/best/best-dehumidifier-brands/) roundup.

faqs.q: What is the best Frigidaire dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For most homes, the FHDD5034Y1 — a 50-pint ENERGY STAR model with Wi-Fi, a 2.7-gallon bucket and auto-defrost to 41°F. If the unit has to sit below the nearest drain, choose a pump model such as the Gallery FGAC5045W1 or the FHDP5033W1.

faqs.q: Is the Frigidaire 50-pint dehumidifier worth it?
faqs.a: Yes, for basements, garages and large rooms. The 50-pint models are ENERGY STAR certified, rated for up to about 4,500 square feet, and the current FHDD5034Y1 is specced at about 470 watts. Pick a pump version (FHDP5033W1, FFAP5033W1 or Gallery FGAC5045W1) if there's no drain lower than the unit.

faqs.q: Is the Frigidaire 22-pint dehumidifier good for a bedroom?
faqs.a: It's the best Frigidaire for one room. The FFAD2233W1 is rated for roughly 330 square feet and one independent review recorded 44.6 dB on low from 10 feet away — quieter than any 50-pint Frigidaire.

faqs.q: Which Frigidaire dehumidifiers have a built-in pump?
faqs.a: Three current models: the Gallery FGAC5045W1, the FHDP5033W1 (also sold as the FHDP5033Y1) and the High Humidity FFAP5033W1. Frigidaire rates the FHDP5033W1's pump for up to 16.4 feet of vertical lift.

faqs.q: What does the EC code mean on a Frigidaire dehumidifier?
faqs.a: On most models it signals a sensor or sealed-system fault rather than a full bucket. Unplug the unit for several minutes to reset it; if the code returns, check the code table in your manual and contact Frigidaire service, especially if the unit is still under warranty.

faqs.q: Where can I find a Frigidaire dehumidifier manual?
faqs.a: Find the model number on the label on the back or side of the cabinet (sometimes behind the bucket), then search it on Frigidaire's support site to download the user manual and parts diagrams.

faqs.q: Does a Frigidaire dehumidifier have a filter?
faqs.a: Yes. Most use a washable mesh filter behind the front grille that you should rinse about every two weeks in heavy use, and some models also take a disposable OEM replacement filter.
